sections.name: toneFor
sections.title: Choosing a colour style for a number
sections.what: Gives a number a style label such as good, bad, warn or neutral, based on words in its field name. Zero always gets neutral.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the summary show status colours without the data sending them.
sections.watch_out: Matching is by substring, so an unrelated field name containing a matched word can be coloured by accident.

sections.name: extractFindings
sections.title: Building the findings list
sections.what: Turns a summary object into a short list of labelled findings. It skips internal keys and skipped names, flattens one level of nested objects, shows lists as item counts, and stops at a set limit, 12 by default.
sections.why: Likely reason: raw summary data is hard to read, so this produces a clean list for display.
sections.watch_out: Text longer than 64 characters is silently dropped, and anything after the limit is cut without warning.

sections.name: fmtClock
sections.title: Showing a clock time
sections.what: Shows a timestamp as local time with hours, minutes and seconds. Shows nothing when no time is given.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps times in the reader's own time zone and format.
sections.watch_out: A badly formed date text shows as an invalid date rather than raising an error.

sections.name: fmtDuration
sections.title: Showing how long something took
sections.what: Shows the gap between two timestamps as seconds, or as minutes and seconds. Shows nothing when either time is missing, and never shows a negative amount.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick sense of how long a step ran.
sections.watch_out: Hours are not shown, so a two hour gap appears as a large minute count such as 120 minutes.

summary: Turns a saved stage summary into a short list of labelled values for display, leaving out build identifiers, hashes and timing numbers.
purpose: Lets the owner see the real results of a stage in plain labels, without technical clutter.
why: The header says only values that literally exist in the summary are shown, and nothing is inferred. This is stated in the code.
how: 1. Keeps a default list of keys that are never shown, such as items, slides and raw. 2. Decides whether a key is technical, based on its name. 3. Turns a key into a readable label. 4. Formats numbers with separators and at most one decimal. 5. Chooses a tone for each value. 6. Collects the findings. 7. Formats clock times. 8. Formats durations. Steps 5 to 8 are not visible in this packet.
inputs: A stage summary object, and an optional extra list of keys to hide.
outputs: A list of findings, each with a label, a display value and a tone. Clock and duration helpers return text.
risks: Name-based rules can hide a real value that happens to end in an id-like suffix. Keys in the default skip list are hidden entirely.
debug: If a value is missing, check the skip list and the technical key rules. If a number looks wrong, check the one-decimal rule. Compare with the test file.
